question: If the expenditure of Company A in 2023 was ₹660 crore and the profit percentage was 35%, then what was its income in 2023?7052
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit % = 35% → Multiplying Factor = 1 + 35/100 = 1.35

Income = Expenditure × 1.35

Income = 660 × 1.35 = 891

**∴ The correct answer is ₹891 crore.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Expenditure = ₹660 crore, Profit % = 35%

Formula: Income = Expenditure × (100 + Profit %)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be70f73a166eae37850c4d13f9e36895e5cf24fb9db68cd2bd17ef358804638f.png] 

⇒ Profit = 35% of ₹660 crore

⇒ Profit = (35 ÷ 100) × 660

⇒ Profit = 0.35 × 660 = 231

⇒ Income = Expenditure + Profit

⇒ Income = 660 + 231

⇒ Income = 891

**∴ The correct answer is ₹891 crore.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit % = [(Income − Expenditure) ÷ Expenditure] × 100. This is the standard formula used for company financial performance.

Loss Percentage Formula

Loss % = [(Expenditure − Income) ÷ Expenditure] × 100. It occurs when expenditure exceeds total income.

Direct Income Relation

Income = Expenditure × [(100 + Profit %) ÷ 100]. This shortcut avoids calculating profit separately.
